title: The Harbor of Sandpiper Point
premise: Edmund Whitlock inherited Sandpiper Point Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and he has trained his heart into obedience: no attachments, no risks, only the ledger. When a freak snowstorm strands his estranged college rival, Julian Marsh, and the woman they both loved and lost, Clara Voss, at the estate, old wounds reopen alongside new tenderness. As thaw approaches and the bank's deadline looms, Edmund must choose between selling the vineyard to save himself or fighting for a future that includes both the land and the people stranded in his care. He learns that survival bought at the price of love is no survival at all — and in the final chapter, he signs the vineyard over to a cooperative led by Clara, choosing to stay as a partner rather than an owner, finally letting someone stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Astrid Lockridge is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade working harvests on the northern coast before turning to fiction. She writes romances about stubborn people and unforgiving landscapes from a cottage she insists is haunted by nothing but drafts.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Losses
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He audits the vineyard's debts on the eve of winter, cataloguing what must be sold to survive the bank's February deadline. A letter arrives announcing an appraiser will visit within weeks. The emotional beat is controlled dread — a man who has made austerity a religion.

chapters.title: What the Train Schedule Knows
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. She boards the last coastal train of the season carrying divorce papers she hasn't signed and a job offer in another country. Her thoughts circle back to Sandpiper Point, where she once spent a summer between two men who destroyed each other over her.

chapters.title: Julian at the Door
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Julian Marsh arrives unannounced, claiming he's scouting the property for investors — investors who would gut the vineyard for its land value. Twenty years of resentment surface in polite, barbed conversation. The beat is two men circling an old battlefield.

chapters.title: Snow Takes the Road
chapters.summary: Clara's POV, stranded mid-route when the train halts; she walks to the only lit building — the vineyard house. Edmund opens the door to find both his ghosts on his porch as the storm seals the road behind them. The beat is vertigo: the past delivered by weather.

chapters.title: Three Plates, One Table
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across the first shared dinner. Forced civility cracks into recrimination: what happened the summer they were all twenty-five, who betrayed whom first. Edmund retreats to the cellar. The beat is the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Cellar Confession
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He finds Edmund among the barrels and admits the truth he's never said aloud: he didn't steal Clara — he let Edmund believe it because losing her friend was easier than admitting Edmund had already chosen the vineyard over everyone. The beat is raw, incomplete honesty.

chapters.title: Frost on the Glasshouse
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. She explores the derelict glasshouse where she once dreamed of planting cuttings and finds Edmund's mother's journals among the ruins — records of debts survived, not avoided. She begins to see Edmund's coldness as inheritance rather than character.

chapters.title: Power Lines Down
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The storm knocks out electricity; the three must share warmth, candles, and rationed food. Working together to save the frost-sensitive vines in the root cellar, their bodies remember old rhythms of trust. The beat is reluctant intimacy through labor.

chapters.title: The Appraiser Calls
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A phone call confirms the appraisal moved up — ten days. Julian reveals his 'investors' are actually a conservation cooperative, not developers, but Edmund refuses to believe anything Julian offers. Pride hardens into a wall. The beat is self-sabotage.

chapters.title: What Clara Signed
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. Julian discovers the unsigned divorce papers; Clara confesses her marriage ended years ago in everything but paperwork, and that she came north to decide whether to disappear abroad or begin again. The beat is a woman reclaiming authorship of her own life.

chapters.title: Kiss in the Cold Room
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Checking the vines at midnight, Edmund and Clara fall into a kiss that undoes twenty years of discipline. Edmund pulls away, terrified — the heart, he insists, is a muscle like any other. The beat is desire colliding with trained denial.

chapters.title: Julian's Long Night
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He witnesses the kiss and walks into the blizzard without a coat, ending up half-frozen at the gatehouse. Edmund drags him back, and tending his old rival's frostbite, feels something shift from hatred to grief for the friendship they buried. The beat is mercy as turning point.

chapters.title: The Journals of Marguerite Whitlock
chapters.summary: Clara reads Marguerite's journals aloud during the blackout: how Edmund's mother mortgaged everything twice and chose love over solvency once, disastrously. Edmund listens and finally understands his fear of attachment was learned, not innate. The beat is inherited pain brought into light.

chapters.title: An Offer Written in Snow
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Recovered, Julian lays out the cooperative's real terms: keep the land working, forgive part of the debt, but Edmund keeps nothing alone. Edmund refuses — ownership is the only identity he has left. The beat is pride choosing poverty over partnership.

chapters.title: The Last Train Before Thaw
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. Roads partially clear; a maintenance train will pass tomorrow. Clara must decide whether to board toward her new life abroad. Edmund, watching her pack, says nothing — and hates himself for it. The beat is silence as betrayal repeated.

chapters.title: Everything the Heart Was Trained For
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Alone with the ledgers, he realizes every sacrifice he's made bought him exactly this: an empty house, dead vines, a closed account. In a fury he burns the debt schedule in the fireplace — then panics, then laughs, then weeps. The beat is breakdown as breakthrough.

chapters.title: Running for the Platform
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund drives Clara through slush to the station as the train idles. On the platform he finally speaks plainly: not a proposal, just the truth — that he wants her to stay, and that staying is the one thing he's never asked anyone for. The beat is vulnerability at full speed.

chapters.title: The Choice on the Platform
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. The whistle blows. Clara steps back from the train and tears up the unsigned papers instead — choosing neither the marriage's ghost nor the escape, but something unmade and hers. Julian, unexpectedly on the platform seeing them off, gives his blessing. The beat is agency, not rescue.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Back at the vineyard, the three draft terms: the cooperative absorbs the debt, Clara brings her viticulture expertise, and Edmund surrenders sole ownership. Negotiations are fierce and honest — the opposite of everything that broke them at twenty-five. The beat is conflict matured into collaboration.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Weeks later, the three work the winter pruning together. Edmund's hands learn the vines again without the weight of ownership, and he discovers that letting go of control has made the land feel more like his than ever. The beat is quiet joy after long austerity.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Clara's POV. The appraiser arrives expecting a desperate seller and finds a functioning cooperative with signed partners and a restoration plan. The valuation holds; the bank agrees to restructure. Julian and Edmund shake hands over the barrel room where they once fought. The beat is the past formally laid to rest.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Epilogue, rotating POV. Spring: the glasshouse rebuilt, first cuttings planted from Marguerite's saved stock. Edmund watches the season's last train pass without longing, Clara beside him, Julian arguing cheerfully about trellising. The heart, he concedes, was trainable after all — he simply trained it wrong. The beat is earned peace.
